summary: Tested 3 new WedSnap features: Couple Invitations, Live Slideshow, Upload Protection (login lockout + guest upload rate limit). Backend: 6/8 pytest tests pass. Frontend: all UI flows for invite couple, magic-link login, /invite/badtoken error, /my-gallery redirect, slideshow (with & without photos), and slideshow controls verified end-to-end via Playwright. Found ONE critical backend bug: login brute-force lockout fails in the deployed environment because request.client.host resolves to the ingress-nginx pod IP (10.81.21.4 / 10.81.21.6) which round-robins across pods, splitting the per-identifier fail counter so the 5-strike threshold is never reached from a single external IP.

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout NOT triggered from external clients. Identifier is built from `request.client.host:email` but in this K8s environment request.client.host is the ingress pod IP and round-robins between multiple pods (observed 10.81.21.4 & 10.81.21.6 in login_attempts collection), so no single identifier accumulates 5 fails. Locally (127.0.0.1) it locks fine on the 5th attempt. Fix: use `request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for','').split(',')[0].strip() or request.client.host` for the IP portion of the identifier.

minor.issue: Upload rate limit (40/60s) uses the same request.client.host — will also be per-pod, not per real client IP. Same fix (X-Forwarded-For) applies. Code path and constants (UPLOAD_RATE_LIMIT=40, WINDOW=60) verified via source. 45 rapid uploads from tester did not trigger 429 (spread across pods).

action_items: HIGH: In /api/auth/login and check_upload_rate(), replace `request.client.host` with the first entry of `X-Forwarded-For` (fall back to client.host). Without this, brute-force lockout and guest upload rate-limit are effectively bypassed in the deployed K8s ingress setup.
OPTIONAL: On the 5th failed login (which sets the lock and returns 401), consider returning 429 immediately so users see the lockout message right away instead of on the 6th attempt.

OPTIONAL: The Slideshow image tile occasionally shows as an empty gold placeholder for a couple seconds while AuthedMedia blob-fetches the file; a subtle loading spinner would improve perceived polish.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py login() and check_upload_rate() trust request.client.host which is the immediate TCP peer. In any reverse-proxy/K8s deploy this is the proxy IP and often round-robins across ingress pods. Must read X-Forwarded-For for meaningful per-client rate limiting/lockout.
accept_invite handles missing/expired token correctly (404/410) and issues httpOnly cookies matching login flow — good.

invite_couple auto-creates a couple user with a random password and 30-day multi-use token — token invalidation on use is not implemented; consider rotating token or single-use if security posture requires.
send_email() surfacing of provider errors: 422 for undeliverable recipients is neatly propagated with a user-friendly reason — good UX.
Slideshow.js polls /api/gallery/{slug} every 12s and shows a 'New memory' toast; works cleanly for restaurant/couple/admin via cookie auth.
InviteAccept.js correctly falls back to invite-error state on 4xx and redirects to /my-gallery on success — solid.

rca of the issue: Login lockout failure RCA: server.py builds identifier as `f'{ip}:{email}'` from `request.client.host`. Under K8s ingress, that value is the internal cluster pod IP of whichever nginx-ingress pod terminated the TCP connection. There are ≥2 such pods, so consecutive requests from the same external client alternate identifiers (observed rows 10.81.21.4:… and 10.81.21.6:… in db.login_attempts). Each identifier tops out at ~2–4 fails, never reaching LOGIN_MAX_FAILS=5. Reproduction: `for i in 1..7; curl POST /api/auth/login with same wrong creds` → all 401. Mitigation: parse X-Forwarded-For (first hop) for the client IP. Same root cause affects check_upload_rate().
